title: Jurassic Park computers in excruciating detail
summary: A deeply technical reverse-engineering analysis of the Sega Genesis Jurassic Park video game, examining the source code, graphics rendering techniques, and computer systems used in the 1993 game adaptation. The article dissects memory management, sprite handling, and the innovative technical solutions developers used to bring Jurassic Park's dinosaurs to life on limited hardware.
problem_solved: Reveals how early 90s developers created impressive game experiences with severe hardware limitations through clever optimization and technical innovation.
why_valuable: Provides rare, detailed insight into retro game development practices and serves as educational material for understanding low-level programming and graphics optimization techniques.
